summary: This note is a list-style summary of Major League Baseball's longest winning streaks and related records. It says the 1916 New York Giants hold the MLB record for the longest unbeaten streak at 26, and that the 2017 Cleveland Indians hold the American League record for the longest winning streak at 22. It also notes that the Chicago Cubs franchise has won 21 games in a row twice, in 1880 as the Chicago White Stockings and in 1935. The text repeats the same points three times with slightly different wording, and only one version says the Indians streak is still ongoing.
one_line: Summary of Major League Baseball's longest winning and unbeaten streak records, including the 1916 Giants, 2017 Indians and Chicago Cubs.
key_facts: The 1916 New York Giants hold the record for the longest unbeaten streak in MLB history at 26.
The 1916 New York Giants' 26-game unbeaten streak included a tie between the 14th and 15th win.
The record for the longest winning streak by an American League team is held by the 2017 Cleveland Indians at 22 games.
One version of the note says the 2017 Cleveland Indians' 22-game streak is still ongoing.
One version of the note describes the 2017 Cleveland Indians' 22-game streak as the second-longest winning streak in MLB history.
The Chicago Cubs franchise has won 21 consecutive games twice.
The Chicago Cubs franchise's first 21-game winning streak came in 1880, when the franchise was known as the Chicago White Stockings.
The Chicago Cubs franchise's second 21-game winning streak came in 1935.
